prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Do you mean (A) a beginner-friendly site that teaches crypto using real, verifiable numbers and charts (on‑chain metrics, TVL, trading volumes, etc.), or (B) an educator or publication that publicly keeps a transparent track record of its own trades and losses (i.e., shows its P&L and admits mistakes)?

If you mean A (data-driven, plain English), good options are:
- Coinbase Learn — very beginner-friendly explainers with simple examples and some data.  
- CoinGecko Learn — beginner guides plus live market data and token pages with real numbers.  
- Glassnode (Glassnode Studio articles) — on‑chain metrics explained in accessible language; shows real realized/unrealized profit and loss metrics (more technical but data-driven).  
- DeFiLlama — simple, plain displays of TVL and changes across protocols (good for learning with numbers).  
- Nansen — wallet-level profit/loss and labeled on‑chain flows (very useful, but mostly paid).

If you mean B (people/sites that openly publish their own losses and a running record):
- That’s much rarer. Individual educators/YouTubers sometimes publish portfolio screenshots, trade recaps and loss posts (look for creators who explicitly keep a public P&L or write “lessons learned” posts). If you want, I can find a few currently active creators who are known for transparent trade recaps.

Tell me which definition you intended (A or B) and whether you want free vs paid tools — I’ll give a short, prioritized list with links and what each does best.
